evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: dark slate node clump fills the top-centre core of the khaki colony while the flanks stay teal-lit; by shot-20s the core is smaller and the dial arrow sits above the 20 cm/s tick.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one line-stroked L-system colony with a flow dial, hairline halos and a dark core; no material, lighting or second layer is visible, so a single rendering idea carries the piece.
evidence.craft: shot-08s: thin teal strokes and hairline halos on flat khaki; the dark core is a dense tangle of overlapping slate strokes that reads as scribble, and the caption sits small at the bottom edge.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: khaki ground with celadon branching coral and no grid, tiles or sand; it differs from the apricot sand grid, dendrite type and ochre Penrose kites of recent nights, though its cream tone is close to the Penrose strip.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: colony centred and fully framed with the dial low; by shot-20s the colony shrinks with clear margin and the dark core persists, so the 20s frame resolves rather than repeating the 2s frame.

pairwise_justification: shot-08s vs median: the Penrose strip has dense ochre and rust kites with strong contrast on cream, while tonight's thin teal strokes on khaki and the dark-slate clump read fainter, so the median wins the vote.

critique.change: At shot-08s replace the overplotted dark strokes in the core with fewer slate node fills and dimmed halos so the stagnant pocket reads as a shaped region with a clear edge rather than scribble.
Add a second rendering idea such as shaded tube depth or soft occlusion on shielded tips, so shot-02s and shot-08s show shelter as light falling off inside the colony, not only as line colour.
Enlarge the 20 cm/s tick and dial readout and let the dial visibly cross it at 6 s, so the threshold reads from the frame itself, not from the small caption at the bottom edge.
